thesis: Frontier AI is a small number of very large pretrained Transformers, built on NVIDIA clusters from web-scale text, aligned on human preference and sold as closed metered APIs behind a chat box. Capability is bought with scale. The models are expensive to run, frozen after training, unreliable in ways they cannot detect, and wait to be asked.

baseline.claim: Frontier capability requires massive centralised compute.
evidence: GPT-4 training compute widely estimated in the tens of thousands of A100-years — 2023-03
Llama 2 trained on a 2,000-GPU A100 cluster — 2023-07
Inflection announces a 22,000-H100 cluster — 2023-06
H100 general availability and sustained shortage through the year — 2023
CoWoS advanced packaging named as the binding supply constraint — 2023

baseline.claim: Transformers are the dominant frontier architecture.
evidence: Every publicly described frontier model of 2023 is attention-based — 2023
Llama 2 architecture disclosure: decoder-only with grouped-query attention — 2023-07
Gemini 1 technical report describes a Transformer — 2023-12

baseline.claim: Capability is primarily produced through pretraining and scaling.
evidence: GPT-4 technical report attributes capability to pretraining scale — 2023-03
Llama 2 reports post-training as behaviour shaping, not capability creation — 2023-07
Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models — 2020-01
Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling — 2022-03

baseline.claim: High-quality human data is the primary training resource.
evidence: RedPajama and SlimPajama reproduce trillion-token open web corpora — 2023-06
Llama 2 trained on 2T tokens drawn from public sources — 2023-07
Llama 2 RLHF built on human preference judgements — 2023-07

baseline.claim: Frontier capability is concentrated in closed providers.
evidence: GPT-4 technical report withholds architecture, data and training details — 2023-03
Claude 2 and Gemini available only as hosted services — 2023
The strongest open-weight model of the year trails the closed frontier on every public benchmark — 2023-12
No frontier model updates weights from deployment — 2023
Retrieval and long context marketed as the answer to knowledge staleness — 2023-11

baseline.claim: Chat and reactive interaction are the dominant interface.
evidence: ChatGPT reaches 100M weekly users — 2023-11
Claude, Bard and Copilot Chat all ship the same surface — 2023
OpenAI DevDay frames assistants as chat threads — 2023-11
The 2023 autonomous-agent wave fails to produce a reliable product — 2023
Function calling framed as a single-turn tool invocation — 2023-06
Stable Diffusion establishes latent diffusion as the open default — 2022-08
DALL·E 3 and Midjourney v5 are both diffusion systems — 2023-10
Stable Video Diffusion extends the same formulation to video — 2023-11

pressures.problem: Frontier training compute is scarce and expensive.
evidence: H100 lead times reported at 6-11 months — 2023-08
CoWoS packaging capacity named as the binding constraint — 2023
Frontier training runs priced in the tens of millions of dollars — 2023

pressures.problem: Running a frontier model is expensive and slow.
evidence: GPT-4 priced at 30x GPT-3.5 per token — 2023-03
Inference described as the dominant lifetime cost of a deployed model — 2023
Latency cited as the blocker for interactive and high-volume use — 2023

pressures.problem: Models are confidently wrong in ways they cannot detect.
evidence: GPT-4 technical report documents persistent hallucination — 2023-03
Calibration degrades after RLHF — 2023-03
Hallucinated citations sanctioned in Mata v. Avianca — 2023-06

pressures.problem: Models cannot reliably complete long multi-step tasks.
evidence: AutoGPT and its successors fail to convert attention into working products — 2023
Per-step error compounds: 95% over twenty steps is roughly 36% end to end — 2023
No production system delegates unsupervised multi-step work — 2023-12

pressures.problem: Frontier capability is controlled by a small number of providers.
evidence: Frontier weights, data and methods undisclosed across all leading labs — 2023
Llama 2's licence restricts the largest commercial users — 2023-07
Researchers cannot reproduce or audit the systems they are asked to evaluate — 2023

pressures.problem: High-quality human training text is finite and legal access is closing.
evidence: New York Times v. OpenAI filed — 2023-12
Reddit and Stack Overflow move to charge for API data access — 2023-06
Projections of high-quality text exhaustion within the decade — 2022-10
Every session begins from the same frozen weights — 2023
Long context and retrieval offered as workarounds rather than solutions — 2023-11
No deployed mechanism for a model to accumulate experience — 2023-12

pressures.problem: Adapting a frontier model to private work is expensive and limited.
evidence: Fine-tuning unavailable on the strongest closed models for most of the year — 2023
Full fine-tuning of an open model requires cluster-scale memory — 2023
Enterprises cite data residency and control as blockers to hosted fine-tuning — 2023
